attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his view.

semantics.note: 'LLMs are peaking' describes the present state, so it is an observation. 'In capability' is the ordinary sense. It has a slight forward-looking flavour, but the observation framing is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'peaking' as gains approaching a plateau, judged on Q2 2024, is ordinary and fair. The speaker gave no measure or threshold, so the reading drives the result.

evidence.note: June 2024 LiveBench: Claude 3.5 Sonnet beats earlier frontier models by about 6%. This is a single-generation gain, so it weighs against a plateau only weakly and does not show sustained broad gains.
June 2024 OlympicArena ranking shows newer models ahead of older ones. It is a one-off snapshot that weighs weakly against stagnation and does not measure the rate of improvement.

reviews.rationale: Both evaluations show newer models in the target quarter beating earlier ones, which weighs somewhat against peaking. But they are snapshots, and neither shows the sustained, broad gains the contradiction condition requires. Nothing shows flattening either. The packet does not settle the trend.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: 'Will not solve' is an unqualified, open-ended negative forecast. The vague scope ('complex problems that actually matter') is kept.

contract.note: The condition is broadly fair, but the result depends on whether an LLM independently reproducing an answer humans had already reached counts as 'solving'. The speaker did not supply that reading, and the contract excludes benchmark success alone.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed Cell paper (online 2025-09-09). The AI co-scientist's top hypothesis matched a mechanism the lab had already confirmed. This is a blind retrodiction test, not the LLM solving an open problem, so it weighs against the claim without clearly meeting the condition.
Institutional news piece establishing the scientific importance of the cf-PICI mechanism. It does not show who solved it.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, so only a conclusive event could settle it. The Cell case is strong, but the researchers solved the problem experimentally first, and the LLM's hypothesis was then checked blind against their answer. That is close to the benchmark-style success the contract says is insufficient, so it does not clearly meet the condition that the LLM materially generated the solution. Not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts this himself, framed as something the media won't accept.

semantics.note: Dropping 'stupid' is fine because it is rhetoric. The rest is a present-state characterization of the sector.

contract.note: Reading 'bubble' as investment exceeding plausible returns, without requiring a collapse, is an ordinary reading. There are no thresholds for big, costly or environmentally destructive, so interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: Sequoia investor analysis (June 2024) on the gap between capex and revenue. It is commentary built on assumptions, covers AI infrastructure broadly, and cannot alone prove a bubble.
Google's own disclosure of 2023 company-wide emissions growth. It covers a different period and does not isolate generative AI.

reviews.rationale: Neither item shows overvaluation against a defensible returns test, or environmental damage attributable to generative AI in Q2 2024. Both are context only. The packet does not settle the compound characterization.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words about OpenAI's models.

semantics.note: The compound observation is kept. 'Authoritatively' is softened, which is a minor loss. The 'all so that' framing of purpose is rhetoric.

contract.note: Assessing the three components separately is fair. Holding the speaker to his literal universal 'not make any businesses any money' matches his own words. The accounting basis for the money component is unspecified.

evidence.note: Independent evaluation of gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, released within the period, found substantial false legal answers. This supports the false-information component only.
2023 water-use modelling paper that notes GPT-4 data was missing. It covers an earlier period and measures nothing attributable to the target quarter.
Klarna's Q1 2024 disclosure reports an 11% cut in operating expenses alongside AI use. It covers a different quarter, has multiple causes, and is not isolated to OpenAI models.

reviews.rationale: The false-information part holds on e1. The environmental part has no measurement attributable to the target period. The money part is neither shown nor refuted: Klarna's figures are not isolated to OpenAI and cover Q1. Two of the three components are unsettled, so the compound claim is unresolved.
